messages:
Devon: Quick heads-up — saw a regression after flipping on the paged-attention GQA/MQA kernel on the A100 ded pool. P99 went up noticeably for our mixed-seq workload.

Hema: Can you paste the perf numbers and the repro steps?

Devon: Repro summary from canary (10k reqs):
```
baseline (streaming legacy kernel): p99=120ms, tokens/sec=19.2k
paged + blocked-kv kernel: p99=140ms, tokens/sec=15.7k
error rate ~ unchanged
```
Model: redwood-open-7b, heads=16, kv_block=128, seq-dist ~ 60%@16 / 30%@512 / 10%@2048

Maria: Interesting — that smells like a cache-layout / kernel mismatch. When KV_BLOCK aligns badly with our block-based attention, we see extra memcpy + stride penalties on Ampere. Did the profiler show memcpy spikes? :thinking_face:

Devon: Yep, nvprof traces show periodic device-to-device copies around certain layers. Timeline looks like the paged kernel is switching to a slow path when stride > 1.

Liam: Two quick ideas: (1) add a cheap online heuristic to pick kernel based on (heads % warp_factor) and expected seq distribution, (2) expand the autotuner sample set to include multi-modal seq lengths.

Maria: Agreed. Proposed kernel-selection rule (pseudo):
```
if (is_gqa && hw.arch == "Ampere") {
  if (kv_block <= 64 || seq_p50 <= 128) use paged_block_kernel;
  else if (kv_block >= 128 && avg_cache_stride > 1.2) use streaming_kernel;
  else fallback to per-layer autotune result;
}
```
That should avoid the memcpy-heavy path for large-block, high-stride cases.

AlexJ: Empirical from my local runs: block=64 -> no regression, block=128 -> p99 up ~15%. So block size matters a lot. We should treat KV_BLOCK as first-class in kernel key.

Naya: We should also persist a small KV-layout fingerprint in the model metadata (head count, kv_block, per-layer block offsets). Autotuner can then warm-start with kernels that historically worked for that fingerprint.

Hema: +1. Also propose adding a new metric to autotuner scoring: cache_stride = mean(bytes_between_successive_kv_accesses) normalized by cache_line. If > threshold, prefer contiguous-friendly kernels.

Liam: For short-term mitigation we can gate paged-blocked on a conservative rule and rollout a canary. Ops — can we run a 5%/10% canary on the A100 pool?

Ops: Yes. Plan: 10% of traffic to ded-a100-canary with kernel-gate enabled (rule from Maria). Rollout window 3 hours, watch p99, tokens/sec, and memcpy/sec. I'll schedule for 30m. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: deploy.started: rollout/kernel-gate/1762508095 -> ded-a100-canary (10%) by Ops

Devon: Thanks. I'll attach the nvprof snippets and a minimal repro script in the ticket. If canary proves stable we can update autotuner to include kv_block as a knob and add the cache_stride metric.

AlexJ: One more datapoint — MQA models (packed heads) behave slightly differently; when we pack heads the stride pattern can get worse. So the autotuner should be architecture-aware and model-layout-aware (GQA vs MQA).

Naya: I'll sketch an autotuner change: sample 3 seq mixes (short-heavy, balanced, long-heavy) and keep best kernel per (model-fingerprint, hw-arch, seq-mix). That should reduce surprises on mixed production traffic.

Hema: Great. If canary shows improvement, let's file a PR to add kv_block to kernel selection keys and add the cache_stride telemetry.

Devon: Cool. I'll post the nvprof logs and a short checklist in the ticket. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
